title: Proposal: Native `<tabs>` Element

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

## Problem
Tabs are one of the most common UI patterns on the web.  
Today, authors must reimplement them using combinations of `div`, `button`, ARIA roles, and JavaScript. This leads to:

- Inconsistent accessibility (keyboard support, focus management, ARIA states often missed).  
- Extra JavaScript for a pattern that could be declarative.  
- Performance and code-size overhead when every site ships its own tab implementation.

The WAI-ARIA specification defines a recommended Tabs pattern, but developers regularly get it wrong.

## Proposal
Introduce a **native HTML ` <tabs> ` element** with child ` <tab> ` and ` <panel> ` elements that encapsulate tab semantics and behaviors declaratively.

### Example
```html
<tabs value="shipping">
  <tab name="shipping">Shipping</tab>
  <tab name="billing">Billing</tab>

  <panel for="shipping">Shipping content…</panel>
  <panel for="billing">Billing content…</panel>
</tabs>
```

### Key behaviors
- **Default accessibility mapping**
  - ` <tabs> ` → `role="tablist"`
  - ` <tab> ` → `role="tab"`
  - ` <panel> ` → `role="tabpanel"` with correct `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby` linkage
- **Keyboard navigation** (roving `tabindex` baked in)
  - Arrow keys move focus between ` <tab> ` elements
  - `Home` / `End` jump to first / last
  - `Enter` / `Space` activate the selected tab
- **State reflection**
  - The `value` attribute on ` <tabs> ` reflects the active ` <tab name=""> `
  - Only the matching ` <panel> ` is exposed/visible to assistive tech
- **Styling hooks**
  - Provide pseudo-elements/`::part` or similar for the tab strip, active tab, indicator, and panel region so authors can style without JS

## Benefits
- **Accessibility by default** (correct ARIA and keyboarding without author code).  
- **Reduced JS boilerplate** and more consistent implementations.  
- **Performance**: smaller pages when the platform supplies the behavior.  
- **Themeable**: design systems can style via parts/CSS without reimplementing logic.

## Alternatives considered
- Continue requiring ARIA patterns + JS: proven to be error-prone.  
- Using `<select>` / `<details>` hacks: do not match tab semantics.  
- Web Components: useful for prototyping, but lack standardized UA-level semantics and consistent a11y across UAs.

## References
- Open UI Tabs research & proposal: `https://open-ui.org/components/tabs`  
- WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: Tabs: `https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabpanel/`  
- Prior WHATWG discussion (example): `https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/199`

---

## Open Questions
- Should ` <panel> ` be a separate element, or should tab content live inside ` <tab> `?  
- Should `value` / `name` be required, or should numeric/index-based activation be allowed?  
- Should we expose a separate ` <tablist> ` element or keep it implicit inside ` <tabs> `?  
- How should animation/indicator hooks be exposed (parts, pseudo-elements, attributes)?

---
